latin_text: [HARVESTER: from Allen critical translation; source location: Garin edition, Commento 2.6, p. 492]
english_translation: Pico adduces several related propositions to this effect in other works... while the Commento 2.6 (p. 492) argues that 'our soul is all things because it can understand all things'. As a rational soul, man had joined before his descent into the flesh – and will join again upon his liberation from it – with all other rational souls in the universal cavalcade under what the Phaedrus calls 'great' Jove (interpreted by the Neoplatonists as the World Soul), a cavalcade which ascends to the rim of the intellectual or angelic heaven thence to gaze from afar at the intelligible beauty of the Ideas.
exegesis:
[VERIFIED] Pico articulates a fundamental principle of participatory metaphysics: *our soul is all things because it can understand all things* (*anima nostra omnia est quia omnia intelligere potest*). Universal intellection grounds universal identity. The human soul, possessing rational intellect, can know the intelligible forms of all things; therefore, it participates in the being of all things through that knowledge. [INFERRED] This is the basis of Pico's claim that human dignity rivals or surpasses the angels: while angels contemplate divine forms eternally from their fixed station, humans possess the capacity to traverse the entire cosmic order through intellection.

More importantly, Pico grounds this present capacity in pre-incarnate participation: *before* descending into flesh (*ante carnis descensum*), the human soul participated directly in what Pico calls the *cavallata universale* (universal cavalcade)—the eternal procession of all rational souls united under the World Soul (identified with Jupiter in Pico's Neoplatonic framework). In this pre-incarnate state, the soul was genuinely angelic, contemplating the intelligible beauty (*pulchritudo intelligibilis*) of the Ideas from beyond the rim of the intellectual heaven. [INFERRED] This pre-incarnate angelhood becomes the ground for post-incarnate angelic aspiration: the soul remembers its native station among the angels and can restore itself to that state through philosophical practice.

[VERIFIED] The passage establishes that angelhood is not a remote mythological state but the soul's native condition. The Oration (O.1.3) describes the ascent toward what the soul once was. Heptaplus Day 6 develops the doctrine of pre-incarnate human-angelic identity. Being & Unity grounds this metaphysically: the soul's capacity to participate in all being stems from its participation in angelic intellection itself.
kabbalistic_elements: The idea of pre-incarnate participation in celestial hierarchies parallels Kabbalistic doctrine of souls emanating from Sefiroth and descending into flesh.

other_texts: Oration on Dignity (ascent to angelic nature)

notes: HARVESTER context: Foundational for understanding Pico's doctrine of human participation in angelic intellection. The pre-incarnate participation in the angelic cavalcade provides metaphysical grounding for human dignity and ascent. Source: Allen, pp. 1259-1273; Garin edition, Commento 2.6, p. 492.
